data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"The append-only log actually requires idempotent writers, not merely safe ones, because deterministic replay demands that the replayed system state match the original state. If retried appends produce duplicate log entries that the original execution did not produce, replay is non-deterministic. Only idempotent writes\u2014achieved through idempotency keys that the log layer deduplicates\u2014ensure that the replayed log is semantically identical to the original.","counterconditions":[{"case":"If the replay protocol already includes a downstream deduplication step (content hashing, sequence-number collapsing), then idempotency at the write layer is unnecessary\u2014the log only needs safe writers","eval":"observation"},{"case":"If deterministic replay is defined as semantic state convergence rather than log-identity, then a downstream idempotent reducer suffices and writers need only be safe","eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the events themselves carry monotonic timestamps or sequence numbers that allow the replay processor to deterministically collapse duplicates, then safe writes plus idempotent processing is sufficient","eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"Consider a writer that appends an event without an idempotency key. Under at-least-once delivery, the same event is appended twice. During replay, the processor sees two entries where the original saw one. If the processor is a state reducer (e.g., summing values), the replayed state differs from the original. This violates deterministic replay. The fix is idempotency keys at the write level: the log (or a deduplication layer) collapses duplicate-keyed entries, making the effective write operation idempotent: f(f(x)) = f(x). Safety alone (no corruption) does not prevent semantic divergence.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
